1 رَتَمَ , (T, S, M, K,) aor.
رَتِمَ , (M, K,) inf. n. رَتْمٌ, (T, S, M, K,) He broke a thing: (ISk, T, S, M, K:) and bruised it, or crushed it, (ISk, T, M, K, TA,) much: (M, and so in the CK:) or, (M, K,) accord. to Lh, (M,) specially, (M, K,) he broke (M) the nose: (M, K: [but see رَتْمٌ, below:]) and رَثَمَ [q. v.] signifies the same: you say, رَتَمَ أَنْفَهُ and رَثَمَهُ [He broke his nose]. (T, S.) ＝
-A2- See also 4. ＝
-A3- مَا رَتَمَ بِكَلِمَةٍ He spoke not a word. (T, S, M, K.) ＝
-A4- رَتَمَتِ المِعْزَى The goats pastured upon the plant called الرَّتَم [in the CK الرَّتْم]. (K, * TA.) ―
-b2- And رَتَمَ He became affected with swooning from eating the plant so called. (K, * TA.) ＝
-A5- رَتَمَ فِى بَنِى فُلَانٍ He grew up among the son of such a one. (K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
